name: viscous_cubesat_nozzle
title: N2 cube-sat nozzle, laminar: discharge coefficient and Isp loss versus Reynolds number (axisymmetric)

reference.quantity: (1 - Cd) sqrt(Re_t) at 10 bar / at 1 bar
reference.source: Laminar boundary-layer scaling delta* ~ Re^-1/2 (Schlichting & Gersten 2017, Boundary-Layer Theory, ch. 6)
reference.shortfall: Flaw of the pre-registered METRIC, not the solver: 1 - Cd (Cd against the 1D choked flow) is dominated by the inviscid 2D throat deficit (Cd about 0.94 at every Re: sonic-line curvature), which does not scale with Re; only the small viscous part does (Cd 0.9413, 0.9433, 0.9441). The viscous loss itself follows the Re^-1/2 scaling: Isp loss against the Euler run 3.20 %, 1.62 %, 0.86 % (local exponents 0.59, 0.54; theory 0.5). Next time pre-register Cd_laminar / Cd_Euler.

reference.quantity: Cd rises with Re_t over the decade (1 = yes, 0 = no)

study.title: Reynolds-number sweep (laminar; Isp loss against the Euler run on the same mesh)
notes: Throat Reynolds number from the sonic throat state, L = D_t.
